clue.text: Sons pick extremely funny person

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in family trees
the pick of something is its cream, the very best part

explanation.surface: Sons choose whoever is the funniest person around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely funny person' reads like a description of the pick, but it is the definition: a scream is a hilarious person.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, someone hilarious is called a scream because they make people shriek with laughter.

clue.text: In church there's female with evil material

indicators.note: the female and evil pieces are placed in the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England abbreviation
a hen is a female bird
ill can mean evil, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: A woman at church is accompanied by wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's' and 'with' are only joining words; the surface reads 'evil' as describing the woman, but it is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Chenille is a tufted, velvety fabric or yarn, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: We face action having sent dad out grabbing 12 land

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take hold of the land piece in their middle
out signals that the letters of sent and dad are thrown into disorder

parts.note: 12 across is MARSHY, and marshy land is a fen

explanation.surface: Someone cheated of land by a father who has been sent away faces legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the seven letters into DEDANTS. The cross-reference must be read with the answer to 12 across (marshy), which makes the land a fen.
explanation.definitionFit: Defendants are those sued or charged, so as a group they are people facing legal action.

clue.text: Fox binds a creature in knot?

indicators.note: the fox word wraps round the letter a, holding it inside

parts.note: tod is an old dialect word for a fox

explanation.surface: A fox ties up some animal in a tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: TOD is a dialect name for the fox; 'binds' puts A inside it. The question mark plays on toad-in-the-hole and the knothole in wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A toad is an amphibian, and the hint of a hole in a knot evokes the dish toad-in-the-hole.

clue.text: Perhaps misuse of semicolons that's not on?

definitions.text: Perhaps misuse of semicolons that's not on?

indicators.note: misusing the letters of semicolons means jumbling them, once the letters of on are removed by not

explanation.surface: Is it unacceptable to misuse semicolons?
explanation.walkthrough: 'misuse of' scrambles SEMICOLONS, and 'not on' removes an O and N from the pool, leaving the eight letters needed. The whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a grammatical blunder, which a wrongly placed semicolon could well be.

clue.text: Wet and muddy planet hastily vacated

parts.note: Mars is the red planet

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outside letters of hastily remain

explanation.surface: A space traveller leaves a soggy planet in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' empties HASTILY to its outer letters, HY.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy ground is boggy, which is exactly wet and muddy.

clue.text: Millions partake of flesh

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
to partake of food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Huge numbers of people share in the flesh of a sacrifice.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal flesh used as food is called meat.

clue.text: Liberal getting in targets Norwegian region

indicators.note: the Liberal letter enters the first target word

parts.note: a tee is a target in quoits and curling
a mark is a target, as in hitting the mark

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician gets into a region with clear targets.
explanation.walkthrough: One plural word gives two separate targets here. Telemark is a Norwegian county that also lends its name to a style of skiing turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Telemark is a county in southern Norway, which gave its name to a skiing style.

clue.text: Coin in grass-covered heap

indicators.note: the informing word covers the heap word, enclosing it

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, also called to sing
a hill is a heap, as in an ant hill

explanation.surface: A coin is found in a mound overgrown with grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is British slang for informing on someone, not the lawn. A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin worth twelve pence.
explanation.definitionFit: The shilling was a British coin worth twelve old pennies until decimalisation in 1971.

clue.text: New lyric poem makes point

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A fresh lyric poem makes its point.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a point where lines or branches meet, as in a network.

clue.text: Preserve business graduate found in tree

indicators.note: the graduate is found inside the tree word

parts.note: the elm is a tree
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: Preserve a business graduate discovered up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a body is to preserve it from decay with chemicals.

clue.text: Bloom's nurse absorbing angry tirade

indicators.note: the nurse word soaks up the tirade, taking it inside

parts.note: an amah is a nurse or maid in East and South Asia
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: Leopold Bloom's nurse takes in an angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Leopold Bloom of Ulysses, but 'Bloom' is the flower. The Asian nursemaid word is a crossword regular; 'absorbing' splits it before the final H.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaranth is a plant with showy flowers, so it is a type of bloom.

clue.text: Thus to have the monarch abdicate?

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a monarch who abdicates goes

explanation.surface: This is why the monarch had to abdicate.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina; the surface invites 'to have the monarch abdicate' as a whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English to mean thus.

clue.text: It might be stuffed poultry she prepared

indicators.note: food that is prepared is worked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook gets the poultry ready for stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed' plays on stuffing a bird, but sofas are stuffed too; 'prepared' rearranges POULTRY SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Upholstery is the padding and covering of furniture, which is stuffed with filling.

clue.text: Rascal's bachelor having shed pounds

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
someone who has lost weight is lighter

explanation.surface: A scoundrel who is a single man has lost weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighter is a mildly abusive British word for a rogue or annoying person.

clue.text: Study fashion in Greater Manchester town

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work
ton is fashion or style, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: A course in fashion is held in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: TON for fashion is a crossword staple from French. Denton is a town east of Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Denton is a town in Tameside, part of the Greater Manchester county in England.

clue.text: Firm to incorporate socialist principles

indicators.note: the firm word takes the socialist into its body

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
red is a colloquial word for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A company takes on socialist principles.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs or principles one lives by.

clue.text: Primitive and others to surround the French soldiers

indicators.note: the others word goes round the French article and soldiers

parts.note: et al. is Latin shorthand for and others
le is French for the
men are soldiers, especially the ranks

explanation.surface: Primitive tribesmen and others encircle French troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to surround' splits the Latin abbreviation for 'and others', putting the French article and the soldiers between its two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental describes something basic or primal, so it can mean primitive.

clue.text: Nuts free to generate capital

parts.note: nuts means crazy, mad
to rid is to free, as in rid of a burden

explanation.surface: Crazy, freewheeling ways generate capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrid is the capital city of Spain.

clue.text: Chairman and protégé posed for screen-shot supremo

indicators.note: posed suggests arranged for a picture, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chairman and his protégé pose for a top film photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posed' rearranges CHAIRMAN and PROTEGE, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinematographer is the chief of camera work on a film, in charge of every shot.

clue.text: Parts taken together for classical musicians

definitions.meaning: a whole made up of parts viewed as one unit
a small group of players performing together

explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is both a whole viewed collectively and a group of musicians who play together.

clue.text: Menacing playwright blows top in Bury

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter goes

parts.note: Harold Pinter's plays are called comedies of menace

explanation.surface: An angry dramatist loses his temper in a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the town near Manchester but is the verb. 'blows top' drops P from PINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body is to bury it.

clue.text: Hit hard at that point in heavy metal

indicators.note: the point word sits inside the heavy metal

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal
there means at that point

explanation.surface: A heavy metal band hits hard at that moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' suggests rock music, but it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathered is British slang for beaten severely, as with a leather strap.

clue.text: Unfinished, Harper Lee's novel about months passing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the months letter
novel means new, so the letters are put into a new order
the first name loses its final letter

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Harper Lee's unfinished novel took months to write.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Harper Lee's late-published novel; here 'novel' is the anagram signal and 'Unfinished' trims only the first name, dropping its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ephemeral lasts only a short time, so it is passing.

clue.text: Cocktail from Guy Busby-Brown?

parts.note: a guy is a man
a busby is a tall fur hat worn by some soldiers
tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: A drink named after someone called Guy Busby-Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: The double-barrelled name splits into three words: a busby is a tall fur military hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a cocktail of whiskey, sweet vermouth and bitters.

clue.text: Come down from Clydesdale?

parts.note: a Clydesdale is a big Scottish draught horse, so stepping off one is getting down from a horse

explanation.definitionFit: To dismount is to get off a horse, and a Clydesdale is a breed of heavy horse.

clue.text: Everyone enthralled by wicked song

indicators.note: held captive by the wicked word, so placed inside it

parts.note: bad means wicked
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone was captivated by a sinful song.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a song, often narrative or sentimental.

clue.text: Gleam on gabled houses between

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the run sits in the words

explanation.surface: Light glints on the gabled houses in between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun among the gables but is the verb that contains the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Among means in the midst of, which is close to between.

clue.text: Temperature, approximately, for body part

parts.note: or so means approximately

explanation.surface: Roughly what temperature is right for a part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body.
